correctness.rationale: Explicit two-point product decomposition proves normalization, positivity, separability and classical-classical character (orthogonal local vectors). F is complex Hadamard and defines exactly mutually unbiased bases; exact rational first/second moments yield variances 187/300 and 1394/2025, covariances 289/900 and 841/2025, hence Pearson sum 51451/46002>1. A direct symbolic 9x9 verifier checks these values. For any separable two-qubit state, covariance of local Bloch components is the classical covariance of the component Bloch vectors; weighted Cauchy-Schwarz and orthogonality of the two local axes bound each local normalized variance sum by 1. Pure-marginal boundary gives zero covariance. The noisy state rho_(1/100) retains a diagonal product-basis form and is full rank; its exact ratios still sum >1. No numerical sampling substitutes for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Maccone, Bruß and Macchiavello arXiv:1408.6851 Section Pearson posed the universal threshold as a conjecture, and the explicit classical-classical qutrit state here violates it by 5449/46002 with no numerical uncertainty. The inspected high-dimensional Pearson studies arXiv:1909.01372 and arXiv:2201.06188 address distinct restricted noisy-state families and even restate the inequality as conjectural; neither gives an all-separable threshold or this counterexample. The later arXiv:2608.03828 reports a two-branch counterexample for mutual-information and conditional-probability functionals, distinct from Pearson, with a partial-access residual risk. This is a statement/implication comparison, not proof of priority by search failure.
residual_risks: The full text of arXiv:2608.03828 was inaccessible; despite different main correlation functional its appendices could contain a previously published equivalent Pearson counterexample.
An equivalent Pearson separability counterexample under alternate observable/outcome labels might be unindexed or described without Pearson terminology.

value.rationale: The 2014 paper explicitly suggested the Pearson sum bound as a universal separability witness; here an exact counterexample has only classical correlations, not entanglement or discord. The accompanying no-qubit-violation theorem makes 3 the sharp first local dimension, while a full-rank classical-classical witness rules out a singular-support artifact. The result explains a genuine false-positive hazard in physically motivated two-MUB entanglement tests, rather than merely calculating an arbitrary matrix. It does not purport to optimize the qutrit violation or settle other correlation criteria.
